item.title: NYPD Still Slapping Street Vendors With Criminal Charges Despite Council Law Requiring Civil Charges
item.description: A police spokesperson said the department was still training officers on the new law.

item.title: Mayor Mamdani Celebrates a Ramadan 'For All of Us'
item.description: It’s important for all New Yorkers, not just Muslims, to see him fully taking part in Ramadan, Mamdani told THE CITY.

item.title: Hochul Reveals How She Wants to Weaken State’s Climate Law
item.description: The governor is urging lawmakers in Albany to make reforms to emissions regulations as the legislature negotiates the state budget.

item.title: Former NYC Taxi Boss Backs Out of Job with Empower, Controversial Ride App
item.description: David Do accepted a job with the tech company for just over a week before making a U-turn.

item.title: Dunkin Donuts Franchisee to Pay $1.5M Over Scheduling Violations
item.description: A probe by city investigators found that Salz Management arbitrarily changed schedules, among other infractions. It now owes 760 workers restitution.

item.title: Mamdani’s New York Is Starting to Take Shape
item.description: The new administration is cutting off the private legal support Eric Adams extended on the city’s behalf to himself and his police officer pals, and rolling out a new Office of Public Safety that’s a far cry from the ambitious Department he’s promised. The FAQ NYC hosts discuss all that and much more, including Zohran […] The post Mamdani’s New York Is Starting to Take Shape appeared first on THE CITY - NYC News.

item.title: MTA Preps for Next Q Line Construction Phase Amid Fed Fund Fight
item.description: The agency is pursuing the next development contract to dig out the trenches for the Second Avenue line’s 106th Street stop.

item.title: Trump-Appointed Judge Keeps City Council Staffer in ICE Detention
item.description: It’s the latest blow for Rafael Andres Rubio Bohorquez, who was arrested in January at an interview in his asylum case.

item.title: NYU Faculty Strike as Union and University Reach Impasse on Wages
item.description: More than 900 non-tenure track NYU professors went on strike on Monday morning, as students returned from spring break.

item.title: Judge Orders Rikers Manager to Fix Jail Woes in 7 Years or Less
item.description: A federal judge has given new overseer Nicholas Deml sweeping powers to reform the jail system, but critics question how long basic rights can wait.
